items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: the bass player, his name was Shakespeare, we called him Shakespeare because he could read his own palm.

ctx.x: Big Maybelle was — I had a day off and I had gone to bed and the bass player, his name was Shakespeare, we called him Shakespeare because he could read his own palm. And he came knocking on the door “Jeannie! Jeannie! Get up. There’s a woman down here made me give her all my money.” I knew, he was so tight, he would tell us, “I’m not buying any Christmas gifts so don’t buy me anything.” That’s how tight he was. So I

knew if she made him give her all his money, I knew that something was really up. So I got dressed really fast and we went down and there were limousines all around this club. We could hardly push our way in. And here was this lady with this baby face. She weighed almost 350 pounds, and she was going through the aisle singing [sings] “Baby please don’t go.” And as she walked she had these pockets, and people were stuffing hundred dollar bills in. And she was still singing. She would hit that hip and make that…
